- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the next 2–3 periods.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule — reduce forecast by 2–4% in the next 3 days if sentiment drops below 0.33.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply a “first-day discount” — reduce first 3 forecast points by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
